column2: How does the search find old-style names, first names, places and dates?
column3: Everywhere (People, ⌘K, Lists, the picker, Where to search?, Duplicates), the search ignores accents, capitals, hyphens and particles (d’Albert = Dalbert = De Albert, Lacombe = La Combe). It understands first names as written in records: abbreviations (J.-Bte, Fçois, Jh, Cath.), Latin forms (Petrus, Joannes, Mariae), diminutives (Toinette) and compounds written as one word (Marianne). For places: St = Saint, “Le Mans” found by “Mans”, and merged communes if the commune history is installed. Dates are typed in French: “vers 1850”, “entre 1850 et 1860”, “avant 1900”, “années 1880”, “XVIIIe siècle”, “3 mars 1850”, “15 brumaire an III”. Exact names come first, then variants; if nothing is found, names that sound the same (“No ‘Dupond’; 3 people close…”). Under each result, “Found by” says why. Settings → 🔎 Search: automatic phonetics, Latin forms, abbreviations, margin for “about”.
